title: Which Protective Order Fits?
summary: Points the victim or family to the right order: DV TRO, SASPA, ERPO or release conditions.

rel.q: Is there a DV relationship between the parties?
rel.help: Current or former spouse or household member, child in common or expected, or a dating relationship.

pred.q: Did a DV predicate act occur (assault, harassment, threats, stalking, criminal mischief, etc.)?

points: Help the victim apply for a TRO (Family Part, or the on-call judge after hours).
Run the mandatory arrest go-by if an offense occurred.
If firearms are a concern, an ERPO can also be sought.
Give the victim DV rights information and resources.
If firearms pose a danger, consider an ERPO.

sex.q: Was the person a victim of nonconsensual sexual contact, penetration or lewdness (or an attempt)?

saspa.result: Sexual Assault Survivor Protection Act order
points: Help the victim apply for a temporary protective order.
Contact SART and the county prosecutor per policy.

gun.q: Does someone pose a significant danger to themselves or others by having a firearm?

points: A family or household member or an officer may petition.
A temporary order can issue the same day.
On service, firearms, ammunition and permits must be surrendered.

charge.q: Is there a pending criminal charge against the person causing the problem?

points: Check whether a judge set no-contact conditions.
Report violations to the prosecutor; in DV cases, they can be charged as contempt.
If there is probable cause, consider harassment (2C:33-4) or stalking (2C:12-10).
A stalking conviction acts as a restraining order (2C:12-10.1).
Refer the person to victim services and civil legal resources.

note: Follow your department's policy and current AG directives. Not yet verified against official sources.
